answer: When k bonded identities equivocate on correlated evidence, the protocol aggregates their attributable faults and applies a penalty proportional to k², rather than treating each as an isolated breach. Escrowed collateral makes each identity costly to operate; detection also triggers asymmetric depreciation, so coordinating a sybil swarm compounds capital loss by an exponential multiplier. A bridge cannot dilute liability, while ripple patterns and cipher proofs help link coordinated acts.
